To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's framing.** The preamble, "[STANDARD]/FINAL" labels and "Reviewer Efficiency Note" are the counterparty's advocacy, not an agreed review protocol. Nothing in our file records principal-level agreement to the limitation or disclosure package, and Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Every clause below has been reviewed in full regardless of the Seller's labels. I'd recommend the cover response expressly state that the "[STANDARD]" designations are not accepted and that all items remain open.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is our conditional fallback and no Amelia Frost written authority exists to deploy it, so the Seller's "agreed at principal level" assertion must be disregarded.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the "excess only" (deductible) mechanic would permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of loss – contrary to playbook.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion; limitations apply to "all Claims" unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations expressly confined to general Warranty Claims.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the "all Claims" wording is a back-door override of the fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity regimes (see SPA-N-014).

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to same caps/time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge qualifier.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Collapsing title into the general regime would cap our recovery on a total failure of title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m purchase; this is non-negotiable.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – no fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the package.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-out.** Purporting to limit liability for fraud is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability; the playbook designates this as non-waivable by anyone on our side.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2]; Sch 7).
- Buyer wants: only specific, fair disclosure (fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope); no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject [1.1]–[1.2]; replace with a fair-disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranty package, and the Seller's own reservation at [11] confirms it has not attempted specific disclosure of conclusions.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers "had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, with the Seller's warranties qualified only by named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Reject; delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" (constructive-knowledge) standard combined with whole-data-room disclosure would make virtually every warranty unclaimable.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter [2] confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being satisfied.
- Buyer wants: condition precedent requiring an effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours.
- Recommendation: **Reject; strengthen to a hard CP.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, so a consent that is delivered but conditional (or ineffective) leaves the core asset at risk; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m facility addressed by release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge of security.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure; repayment directly from Completion funds; executed and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release.** We would otherwise acquire an encumbered company with a lender holding change-of-control rights (cl 8.1) and no legal certainty of discharge; a post-completion release is only tolerable with an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which exists.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DD-005)**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter [5] confirms they are absent from the flow and silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: the AUD 420,000 **plus** all triggered on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, leave accruals) as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller, or treated as a Completion deduction/Debt-like item.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require express line item.** Without it, Paperbark (i.e. the Buyer) bears a ~AUD 420,000+ liability that is triggered by the Seller's transaction, undermining the debt-free/cash-free bargain.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter [4]: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering (i) any failure of title to or infringement claims over Ironquay-developed materials, (ii) costs of obtaining confirmatory assignment, (iii) loss from any resulting customer/product disruption – while preserving the SOW3 payment cure route; plus a pre-Completion deliverable of paid receipt and executed assignment.
- Recommendation: **Reject as drafted; broaden.** The real exposure is IP ownership of delivered software, not the AUD 180,000 fee, and that figure is unverified in either direction – the indemnity should follow the risk, not the invoice.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). Disclosure Letter [6]: ~1,240 records sent to unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no loss stated.
- Buyer wants: covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation pre-Completion with Buyer visibility; ongoing update obligation; specific indemnity for regulatory, notification and third-party costs arising from the incident; no admission or assumption either way.
- Recommendation: **Reject materiality characterisation; add investigation covenant and specific indemnity.** The Seller's own disclosure concedes the key facts are unknown, so "not material" is a conclusion without evidence – we neither accept it nor assert a confirmed breach, but we must not inherit the uncharacterised risk under a 20% cap.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter [8]: three AUD 110,000 renewals (DD-008, DD-011) to be read together; silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: DD follow-up to establish timing, scope, termination rights and whether any amount is accrued/pre-paid before Completion; then assess treatment.
- Recommendation: **Hold open – neither accept nor classify.** Consistent with the playbook there is no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction, but we cannot accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label when its own letter declines to assert that.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: single general regime for everything – cl 12.3/13 "applies to all Claims", cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature", Tax/IP "settled under the general regime", title folded in.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations (price, Riverlark, bonuses, leakage) and covenants each in their own regime with their own cap and period; a drafting rule that general limitations apply **only** where expressly stated.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft with express category separation.** The Seller's cumulative "all Claims" language is a hidden override that would import the 20%/18-month regime into every head of recovery including price adjustment and specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] concedes the register is merely the "source relied on" and that Buyer has not completed verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member/charges search, PPSR search, review of constitution and share issue/transfer documents, board/shareholder approvals, confirmation of no options/convertibles or encumbrances; title and authority warranties on the fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient; complete independent verification before signing.** An internally maintained register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof of ownership, encumbrance status or authority.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considers tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN and negotiated separately – tax covenant/indemnity with its own cap and period (typically to statutory limitation plus buffer), IP warranties with a separate cap; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; record as OPEN.** Tax and IP are the two highest-exposure areas for a SaaS target (and Ironquay/DD-006 already show IP and data risk), so they cannot be swept into a 20%/18-month regime by assertion.

---

### Summary for the deal team
- **Reject:** 001, 002, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009, 010, 011, 014, 015 (as sufficient), 016 (as "settled").
- **Hold open / further DD:** 012 (investigation + indemnity), 013 (Sandbar), 015 (verification work), 016.
- **No fallbacks deployed:** the 20% cap and 18-month period both require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft; none exists, so our counter is 25% / AUD 6.0m and 24 months.
- **Immediate actions:** (i) written response rejecting the "[STANDARD]/FINAL" framing; (ii) commission ASIC/PPSR title searches; (iii) request Riverlark payout letter and Bluefen cl 11.3 condition evidence; (iv) request Ironquay payment receipt/assignment, DD-006 investigation logs and Sandbar contract terms.

- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft with express category separation.** The Seller's cumulative "all Claims" language is a hidden override that would import the 20%/18-month regime into every head of recovery including price adjustment and specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter [10] concedes the register is merely the "source relied on" and that Buyer has not completed verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence – ASIC extract and historical member/charges search, PPSR search, review of constitution and share issue/transfer documents, board/shareholder approvals, confirmation of no options/convertibles or encumbrances; title and authority warranties on the fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).
- Recommendation: **Do not accept DD-012 as sufficient; complete independent verification before signing.** An internally maintained register supplied by the Seller is not independent proof of ownership, encumbrance status or authority.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: considers tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN and negotiated separately – tax covenant/indemnity with its own cap and period (typically to statutory limitation plus buffer), IP warranties with a separate cap; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- Recommendation: **Reject "settled"; record as OPEN.** Tax and IP are the two highest-exposure areas for a SaaS target (and Ironquay/DD-006 already show IP and data risk), so they cannot be swept into a 20%/18-month regime by assertion.
